title: Control method for electromagnetic chuck device, and electromagnetic chuck device

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.quote: The electromagnetic chuck device 60 includes an electromagnetic chuck main body 61, eight pairs of suction support members 62 and 63, and a control device 64.
features.note: The reference discloses an electromagnetic chuck main body (housing) and suction support members (pole shoes) but does not explicitly mention a displaceable magnet within the housing. It mentions magnetizing pole portions by supplying current to coils.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.note: The reference describes magnetizing pole portions by supplying current to coils, implying an electromagnet, but does not describe a physically displaceable magnet.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: The eight pairs of suction support members 62 and 63 according to the present invention are provided on the upper surface of the face plate 61 a of the electromagnetic chuck main body 61.
features.note: The reference describes 'suction support members' (pole shoes) attached to the 'electromagnetic chuck main body' (housing), with 'upper surfaces' that contact the workpiece.
features.refuted: The quote states that suction support members are on the upper surface of the face plate, not that pole shoes are attached to the housing. It also doesn't mention pole shoes.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: Thereby, a magnetic force is generated satisfactorily on the upper surfaces 62c and 63c of the adsorption support members 62 and 63, and a sufficient adsorption force for the workpiece W can be obtained.
features.note: The reference describes the design of the suction support members (pole shoes) and their upper surfaces (workpiece contact surfaces) to generate sufficient magnetic force for adsorption, implying guiding the magnetic field.
features.refuted: The quote describes the generation of magnetic force on the upper surfaces of the adsorption support members to obtain sufficient adsorption force, but it does not state that pole shoes are designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: The reference does not mention a 'displacement direction' for a magnet, nor does it specify a 'contact surface angle' in relation to such a direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: The reference describes a magnetic chuck with a housing and pole shoes, but lacks a displaceable magnet and a specified contact surface angle relative to a displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.quote: The electromagnetic chuck device 60 attracts a work piece W by magnetic pole parts 71 to 78.
features.note: The reference describes an electromagnetic chuck device that attracts a workpiece using magnetic force, which implies the workpiece is pressed against contact surfaces.
features.refuted: The quote states that the electromagnetic chuck device attracts a workpiece by magnetic pole parts, but it does not describe a magnet in gripping position pressing the workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force. It also doesn't mention a magnetic gripper system.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.note: The reference describes the electromagnetic chuck main body as having a central axis (G-axis) but does not mention a displaceable magnet or its displacement direction.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.quote: The upper surfaces 62c and 63c are portions that suck and fix the attracted surface Wa of the workpiece W that comes into contact therewith.
features.note: The reference describes the specific shape and arrangement of the upper surfaces of the suction support members (pole shoes) to effectively support and fix the workpiece, implying an active structure for directing the magnetic field.
features.refuted: The quote describes the upper surfaces as portions that suck and fix the attracted surface of the workpiece, but it does not state that pole shoes have an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: In addition, the upper surfaces 62c and 63c are formed so that the side opposite to the side facing the opposing surfaces 62b and 63b is inclined from the outer peripheral side of the face plate 61a toward the direction
features.note: The reference describes the upper surfaces (workpiece contact surfaces) of the suction support members as being inclined, which constitutes a bevel. While a specific angle range is not given, the presence of an inclination is disclosed.
features.refuted: The quote mentions that the upper surfaces are inclined, but it does not specify an active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference describes the upper surfaces of the suction support members as contact surfaces but does not mention multiple projections forming these surfaces.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: The reference does not describe multiple projections or recesses on the contact surfaces of the pole shoes.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.quote: The workpiece W may be carried in, reversed, and carried out manually by the operator, and the center alignment in that case is performed using a jig or the like.
features.note: The reference mentions using a jig for center alignment when manually positioning the workpiece, which is a positioning device. However, it is not explicitly described as 'on the magnetic gripper'.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.quote: The magnetic pole part 76 (N pole) and the magnetic pole part 77 (S pole) through which the magnetic flux passes under the control of the control device 64 are composed of combinations of different magnetic poles (N pole and
features.note: The reference explicitly states that adjacent magnetic pole parts are controlled to become N and S poles, which corresponds to the first and second pole shoes acting as north and south poles.
features.refuted: The quote mentions N pole and S pole magnetic parts, but it does not describe a magnet in gripping position making the first pole shoe act as a north pole and the second as a south pole. It refers to magnetic pole parts, not first and second pole shoes.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.note: The reference describes controlling magnetic force by energizing coils, not by displacing a magnet.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.quote: Specifically, for example, an AE sensor 65 is attached to each of the pair of suction support members 62 and 63 (see FIG. 3).
features.note: The reference describes using an AE sensor to detect contact between the workpiece and the suction support members, which functions as a workpiece sensor.
features.refuted: The quote states that an AE sensor is attached to each pair of suction support members, but it does not specify that it is a position sensor detecting gripping/release position or a workpiece sensor detecting a ferromagnetic workpiece.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.quote: Specifically, for example, an AE sensor 65 is attached to each of the pair of suction support members 62 and 63 (see FIG. 3).
features.note: The reference states that an AE sensor is 'attached' to the suction support members, implying a mounting point, but does not explicitly describe a 'receptacle' in the housing for receiving the sensor or a supply line.

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.quote: At this time, the workpiece W is carried in by a robot (not shown). The robot is configured to carry the workpiece W in a state where the center axis of the workpiece W is aligned with the rotation center
features.note: The reference mentions a robot carrying the workpiece to the electromagnetic chuck, implying an interaction, but does not explicitly describe a 'manipulator interface' on the chuck itself.

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.note: The reference discusses magnetic flux leakage between pole shoes but does not describe any specific housing design or shielding device to suppress magnetic field escape from the housing itself.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference does not describe projections on the pole shoes, nor does it relate any dimensions of the pole shoes to the workpiece thickness.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.note: The reference does not describe any grooves in the housing.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: In addition, the upper surfaces 62c and 63c are formed so that the side opposite to the side facing the opposing surfaces 62b and 63b is inclined from the outer peripheral side of the face plate 61a toward the direction
features.note: The reference discloses an inclination (bevel) on the workpiece contact surface but does not specify a bevel angle or a range of 15° to 75°.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference discloses an inclination (bevel) on the workpiece contact surface but does not specify a bevel angle, let alone a range of 40° to 60°.
